knowledge-base.overview: SwiftUI 5.0+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for iOS 17+, macOS 14+, watchOS 10+, tvOS 17+, and visionOS 1.0+. Covers declarative view composition, state management with @Observable, NavigationStack with typed routes, TabView, List/Grid patterns, async data loading, custom modifiers, environment-based DI, forms, previews, and XCTest view model testing. Applies to .swift files using SwiftUI.

core-principles.principle: Describe what the UI should look like; SwiftUI handles all rendering. Never imperatively mutate view state outside of state wrappers.
Each piece of state lives in exactly one place. Views derive their display from state — they do not maintain their own copy.
Keep views small and composable. Decompose body into private computed properties at 30+ lines. Extract reusable pieces as separate structs.
Use @Observable (iOS 17+) for view models instead of ObservableObject/Published. @State owns the instance; @Environment passes it down the tree.
Use .task modifier for async data loading. It automatically cancels the task when the view disappears — no manual cancellation needed.

guardrail.rule: Never mutate @State or @Observable properties during a view update cycle (synchronously inside body). Only mutate in event handlers, .task, or .onChange callbacks.
Never create @StateObject in a computed property. @StateObject must be created at the stored property level — computed properties are recreated on every render.
guardrail.bad: var viewModel: UserViewModel { UserViewModel() } // recreated every render

guardrail.rule: Never use @ObservedObject for state the view owns. Use @StateObject (iOS 14-16) or @State with @Observable (iOS 17+) for owned instances.
guardrail.bad: @ObservedObject var viewModel = UserViewModel() // view owns it but uses wrong wrapper
guardrail.good: @State private var viewModel = UserViewModel() // iOS 17+ with @Observable

guardrail.rule: Keep views under 200 lines. Decompose body into private computed properties using // MARK: - Subviews at the 30-line mark.
Never perform heavy computation inside body. Precompute in view models, use .task for async work, or cache with stored properties.
guardrail.good: private var filteredNames: String { /* computed once */ } var body: some View { Text(filteredNames) }

guardrail.rule: Use LazyVStack / LazyHStack for long scrollable lists. Use LazyVGrid / LazyHGrid for grids. Never use VStack/HStack for unbounded data.
Avoid AnyView type erasure. Use @ViewBuilder, Group, or generic constraints instead. AnyView suppresses diff optimizations.
Use NavigationStack with typed Route enum for navigation. Avoid legacy NavigationView (deprecated iOS 16+).
Provide multiple #Preview configurations: light mode, dark mode, different devices. Include static preview data via extension on model types.
Use environment-based dependency injection for testability. Define custom EnvironmentKey types and inject mock implementations in previews and tests.

notes.note: Features/ groups by domain with Views, ViewModels, Models, Components
Shared/ for cross-feature reusable views and custom modifiers
Core/ for non-UI infrastructure: networking, storage, extensions
